title: Dark Matter and Dark Energy: The Unknown 95% of the Cosmos
executive_summary: Normal atomic matter accounts for only about 5% of the total mass-energy content of the universe. Dark matter makes up approximately 27%, providing the gravitational glue that holds galaxies together, while dark energy accounts for ~68%, accelerating cosmic expansion. This topic provides an essential, rigorous framework for understanding Dark Matter and Dark Energy: The Unknown 95% of the Cosmos within modern astrophysics, space exploration, and theoretical physics. By investigating foundational physical mechanics, observational data, historical milestones, and future technological challenges, this comprehensive guide offers a thorough 800-1000 word overview designed for in-depth mastery of the subject. key_sections.title: 1. Observational Evidence for Dark Matter
key_sections.content:
Dark matter is inferred from galactic rotation curves, gravitational lensing of distant galaxy clusters, and acoustic peaks in the Cosmic Microwave Background. key_sections.content:
